headline: SILVER SURGES 3%: White metal rebounds to $77.66/oz as US-Iran peace talks ease inflation fears
snippet: Silver climbed to $77.66/oz on Monday, up 3.07%, recovering recent losses as optimism over a potential US-Iran agreement eased fears of an energy-driven inflation shock that could force rates higher. The white metal is 36% below its January all-time high of $121.64 but holding above key support levels as the sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit provides a fundamental floor.

headline: TIGHTER THAN OPEC: China's rare earth grip spans missiles to iPhones — and didn't loosen after Trump-Xi summit
snippet: Real Alloys' CEO argues China's dominance over rare earth processing is structurally tighter than OPEC's oil cartel ever was — covering defence-grade alloys, consumer electronics, and EV magnets simultaneously. The interview arrives days after the Trump-Xi summit showed little sign of Beijing easing its critical mineral export controls, with indium exports to the US down 77% since February 2025.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,700: Central banks bought 244 tonnes in Q1 — fastest accumulation pace in over a year — despite record prices
snippet: Gold is consolidating in the $4,650–$4,750/oz range as the Middle East conflict sustains safe haven demand while US-Iran peace negotiations introduce two-way volatility. The World Gold Council's Q1 2026 data shows central banks spent $37 billion on gold last quarter — the highest-value single quarter on record — with 68% of central banks planning further additions to reserves this year.

headline: COPPER AT $6.28: AI data centres need 3–4x more copper than conventional facilities — structural deficit building
snippet: Copper futures hit $6.28/lb this week, up 2% in a session, as accelerating AI infrastructure buildout amplifies already tight mine supply — a single large AI facility requires up to 50,000 metric tonnes of copper versus 12,000 for a conventional data centre. J.P. Morgan estimates data centre copper demand alone could reach 475,000 metric tonnes in 2026, with Chile's Cochilco raising its 2026 average price forecast to $5.55/lb.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $84.70: Meta locks up 7.8 GW of nuclear, Microsoft adds 800 MW — tech giants reshaping the supply curve
snippet: Uranium spot held at $84.70/lb as unprecedented demand signals from hyperscalers pile onto utility re-contracting needs — Meta signed agreements for up to 7.8 gigawatts of nuclear capacity and Microsoft secured 800+ megawatts exclusively for AI data centre operations. Denison Mines' Wheeler River Phoenix deposit is now in early construction, the first new Canadian uranium mine permitted in over two decades.

headline: COT REPORT MAY 22: Weekly CFTC gold, silver and USDX positioning — where speculative money is parked
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly CFTC Commitments of Traders roundup for May 22 maps net speculative positioning in gold and silver futures alongside the US Dollar Index — the key gauge of institutional momentum heading into the next leg of the precious metals cycle. Published as gold consolidates in the $4,650–$4,750 range and managed money reassesses the trade after the brutal correction from January's $5,405 record.

headline: BEST EVER DRILL: GR Silver hits 45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag at San Marcial — "best hole in the deposit's history"
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) reported hole SMS26-04 at Mexico's San Marcial project — 45.1m true width at 1,623 g/t silver including a stunning 8.25m at 8,579 g/t Ag — calling it the best result in the deposit's history. The company is advancing a 20,000m 2026 drill campaign at a project carrying 134 million silver-equivalent ounces of existing resources.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER: 51.5m at 890 g/t AgEq at Boumadine — new parallel structure found 70m below pit shell
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) drilled 890 g/t silver equivalent over 51.5 metres at Boumadine in Morocco — including 1,504 g/t AgEq over 19.3m — and one hole cut a new mineralized parallel structure 70 metres below the current resource pit shell. Results confirm the Boumadine Main Trend is both high-grade and open at depth, pointing to further resource growth.

headline: AUSTRALIA FORCES CHINA OUT: Six Beijing-linked investors ordered to sell Northern Minerals heavy rare earth stakes within 14 days
snippet: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers gave six Chinese-linked entities a fortnight to sell their combined 17.58% stake in Northern Minerals, owner of the Browns Range dysprosium-terbium project — one of the few heavy rare earth operations outside China's downstream control. Northern Minerals shares fell 13.8% on the announcement; Beijing called the move discriminatory as Australia's FIRB accelerates strategic mineral reviews.

headline: NDPR PULLS BACK 21% FROM Q1 PEAK: Rare earth prices consolidating — but Western producers remain profitable
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg after a record Q1 rally, with analysts projecting a $95–$115/kg consolidation range through Q2 2026. MP Materials and Lynas Rare Earths remain well above their cost bases at current prices, while the US government's DoD-backed $110/kg NdPr price floor provides policy-supported downside protection for domestic production.

headline: TROILUS MINES NEW ZONE: 2.92 g/t AuEQ over 19m outside current resource at Quebec copper-gold project
snippet: Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG) announced first results from the West Rim Zone at its Quebec copper-gold Troilus project — 2.92 g/t gold equivalent over 19 metres sitting entirely outside the current NI 43-101 resource. The company is running a 40,000m 2026 drill campaign targeting resource expansion at a project already hosting a multi-million ounce gold-equivalent resource in a Tier 1 jurisdiction.
